Mean by visit: a figure from the template mean_se or mean_ci

Source: R/tpl_fig.R
tpl_mean_se.Rd

The A use of a figure's template SPEC: the program makes the records (the dataset read, the analysis set's subjects kept, the parameter, the records with a value and a visit, the visits in their order), then one call draws the mean of each group at each visit, a line and points, with bars of +/- one standard error (mean_se) or the 95% confidence interval (mean_ci). The means are made here, from the records. A report's own layers and settings go after the call with +.

Usage

tpl_mean_se(
  data,
  group = "TRT01A",
  value = "AVAL",
  visit_var = "AVISIT",
  visit_order = "AVISITN",
  param = NULL,
  plot = NULL
)

tpl_mean_ci(
  data,
  group = "TRT01A",
  value = "AVAL",
  visit_var = "AVISIT",
  visit_order = "AVISITN",
  param = NULL,
  plot = NULL
)

Arguments

data

The records: one a subject and visit, the parameter's.

group

The lines' variable (TRT01A), bare or as text.

value

The variable averaged (AVAL, CHG).

visit_var

The visits on the x axis (AVISIT), a factor in their order.

visit_order

The visits' order (AVISITN).

param

The parameter, for the y axis' title; NULL: none.

plot

The figure's settings over the template's (x_label, y_by, legend ..., as a designed figure's plot:).

Value

A ggplot.

See also

tfl_template_expand() for the design it draws (the B use).

Examples

saf <- adsl$USUBJID[adsl$SAFFL == "Y"]
df <- advs[advs$PARAMCD == "SYSBP" & advs$USUBJID %in% saf, ]
df$AVISIT <- stats::reorder(factor(df$AVISIT), df$AVISITN)
p <- tpl_mean_se(df, group = TRT01A, param = "SYSBP")
class(p)
#> [1] "ggplot2::ggplot" "ggplot"          "ggplot2::gg"     "S7_object"      
#> [5] "gg"
